report:
Reviewed the complete canonical_outputs claim, all six implementation associations and all three test entries. Captured the solver design, accepted goal-specific-output RFD and crate/trait lookup plus in-memory setup helpers. Source inspection only; no tests rerun and no source changes.

The claim distinguishes Prove(P)->Proven from input-only Normalize(Alias)->Type, requires output variables to participate in all canonical-response operations and forbids expected-type-directed candidate choice before merging. goal.rs models the operation explicitly and normalization carries only the alias; result.rs includes GoalOutput in a successful canonical response alongside substitution and residual goal, with response-local binders carrying universe/domain metadata. boundary.rs checks operation/output kind compatibility before extraction, copies substitutions, output and residual through one extractor, binds response variables and validates that no proof-local InferVar escapes. Its caller import uses the response binder/mapping and imports the output with the rest of the answer. goal.rs's tracked solve result includes this output-bearing response, so output is part of cached semantic knowledge rather than a separately inferred caller convention.

prove.rs normalization constructs candidate type outputs and merges complete candidate answers. merge.rs restricts the unconditional-proof shortcut to Proven with empty substitution/trivial residual and compares Type outputs when checking candidate subsumption; an arbitrary unconditional type is not a universal proof. infer_ctx.rs apply_normalization_relation receives the solved response, imports it transactionally, and only then relates its Type output to the caller expectation; Maybe/No returns discard rather than choosing a candidate matching that expectation. These six files provide the intended output flow, but inspection alone does not prove every variable-sharing/universe/cache/merge edge case.

canonical_response_rejects_an_output_for_the_wrong_operation deliberately builds a Prove(true) state and tries to extract a successful Type(bool), requiring the exact incompatible-output panic. This tests extraction rejection, not every malformed caller-import combination. local_associated_type_normalization_produces_a_type_output constructs the actual Iterable::Item projection for Wrap<bool>, canonicalizes input-only Normalize, invokes the solver and requires Yes with Type(bool), empty substitution and trivially true residual. Captured helpers obtain real local crate/trait identities and parse source, so the test exercises actual associated-type normalization rather than a fabricated response.

The solver_canonical_outputs TODO retains repeated response-local variable round trips with sharing/universes, incompatible outputs staying ambiguous despite a caller preference, and proof outputs not exposing a selected impl identity, along with complete mismatch validation. Its prerequisite is that broader canonical-output matrix, including caching/comparison/import behavior beyond the concrete bool case. It has no assertions and remains deferred evidence. All implementations/tests and every claim category are accounted for; the two ordinary cases are not promoted to exhaustive canonical-boundary proof. No concrete defect was identified in these inspected paths and no additional edits are requested.
